messages:
evan: Pager fired for high 5xx rate on /v1/generate from APAC region. Alert spike started ~1960012320, currently ~12% 5xx over baseline. I’m triaging now.
ops-bot: Incident opened: INC-2026. Severity: SEV2. Pager duty notified. Initial responders: evan.
anya: On it — looking at the runtime logs, I see a lot of KVCACHE misses and some grpc timeouts to model-host-3. Can you paste the curl to hit the health endpoint?
evan: 10-4. quick check: `curl -sS https://runtime-apac.internal/health | jq .` — returning OK for host-1/2, host-3 is slow (connect timeout).
matt: I’m re-routing minimal traffic via the canary policy to model-host-2 to buy time: `rwctl route set --policy canary --backends host-2` — should be immediate. Watching metrics.
ops-bot: Action taken: traffic re-route applied by matt. Estimated mitigation time: now.
evan: traffic looks stabilized, 5xx down to ~2%. Good temporary mitigation. Still need root cause for host-3 connection failures.
kevin: +1 on looking at host-3. Oncall runbook suggests checking nvlink and docker restarts — can someone SSH to host-3 and share dmesg?
tara: I’m on host-3 now. Found repeated OOM killer events for the shard process, and the GPU memory usage spiked before the kernel OOM. Suspect model batch explosion after a long prompt.
iris: Customer impact check: support-tickets show three customers reported timeouts (ticket RW-4271, RW-4276, RW-4278). I've flagged as high priority and started outreach.
evan: Thanks. I’ll escalate to Dedicated SRE for a deeper dive and open a post-incident thread. For now we’ll keep the auto-route in place and create a rollback if the host comes back flaky.
pagerduty-bot: Incident update posted to on-call channel and stakeholders. CC: product, sales.
anya: Quick remediation actions: 1) limit max_batch_size on host-3 to 8; 2) add a guard to drop requests with sequence_length > 8k for that cluster; 3) create alert for GPU memory overtime growth. Assigning owners below.
matt: I’ll create the guard PR and roll it to canary tomorrow AM. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5421
kevin: I’ll own the GPU OOM tracker alert (RW-5234). Setting up alert rule and dashboards.
tara: I’ll open infra ticket to investigate docker runtime config and node-level mem cgroup limits (RW-5235).
evan: Postmortem planning: can we meet TOMORROW 1400 UTC for a 40 min review + action assignment? I’ll create the doc and invite SRE, runtime, infra, product, and support. Proposed doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/incidents/INC-2026-runbook-draft — feel free to add notes.
anya: Works for me. I’ll prepare a short repro and the log snippets.
iris: I’ll summarize customer communications and include timelines in the doc.
matt: For brown-bag shareout, I can present the mitigation pattern (traffic re-route + canary). Who wants to pair on the slides? :thumbsup:
evan: I can help with slides. Let’s reserve 30m in next week’s engineering all-hands slot for the learnings cascade.
ops-bot: Post-incident checklist created and linked: RW-5236. Items: RCA, runbook updates, owners assigned, follow-up training.
evan: Action items recap (adding to doc): - RW-5234 (kevin): GPU OOM alert + dashboard. - RW-5235 (tara): Node mem cgroup investigation + infra fixes. - PR-5421 (matt): request guard for long sequences (deploy to canary). - RW-5236 (ops-bot): Post-incident checklist and runbook update. - RW-5237 (anya/evan): Postmortem doc + customer timeline.
kevin: ETA for alert and dashboard: EOD tomorrow.
tara: Infra ticket prioritized, ETA 3 days for config change in non-prod, 7 days for prod rollout.
anya: I’ll attach the key log snippets to the postmortem doc and add a short script to reproduce the batch behaviour.
matt: brown-bag slot request created: Thursday 1500 UTC — calendar invite to follow.
evan: Closing the live mitigation thread: current status stable, mitigation (traffic re-route) remains in place until PR deploys. Postmortem meeting scheduled. Thanks everyone for the quick response :heart:
